attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: Joint capability work and knowledge exchange can expose or repair a concrete inability to meet the interface contract, while including supplier burden and proprietary limits.
Actual capability evidence and shifted-cost accounting affect how much joint investment is justified before the next learning result.
Supplier-side workload, training, lock-in and viability enter the estimate, exposing gains that are only a transfer from supplier to buyer.
Actual technical openness, capability and fair risk allocation inform whether the dependency can meet commitments and whether imposed requirements are sustainable.
Verified supplier competence and workable escalation supply one support-readiness premise, including whether burdens make the promised response credible.
A demonstrated supplier capability and feasible escalation route can provide a concrete restoration task or alternate output in the recovery plan.
Capability, viability and fair continuing allocation inform whether the supplier can maintain the actual fielded configuration rather than only initial delivery.
Actual competence, bargaining burden and dependency risk change the consequence/cost assessment of proposed supplier controls.
